tables.explanation: Execution stage: The hierarchical MAML pipeline (hierarchical_meta_learning_pipeline.py) cannot be executed because the required TCGA RDS data files are entirely absent from the repository. No MAML model checkpoints exist. The only few-shot results in the repository come from a simple nearest-neighbor classifier (simple_meta_learning_analysis.py), which produced an average 5-shot accuracy of ~85.3% across 5 cancer types — close to but not the claimed 85.7%, and from a fundamentally different method than the paper's 'Full Model'. Without the TCGA data or trained MAML checkpoints, the claim of 85.7% 5-shot accuracy for the Full Model cannot be verified or refuted.

results_section.explanation: Execution stage: The claim requires both a hierarchical MAML 1-shot evaluation (70.2%) and a standard MAML baseline (45.1%). The hierarchical MAML code exists but cannot run due to missing TCGA data. More critically, 'standard MAML' is described as a baseline in the manuscript but has no implementation in baselines.py or elsewhere in the codebase. No 1-shot result artifacts exist in any pkl or JSON file. Since there is a plausible code path for hierarchical MAML (blocked by data) but no concrete code/execution conflict that definitively contradicts the paper, this falls under Insufficient Evidence rather than fabrication.
